original_question: Is there a structural criterion that decides when the tensor product A tensor_F B of two F-division algebras contains a zero divisor, equivalently when it fails to remain a division algebra?
target_in_paper: Section 9, Problem 9.1 (p. 25): "Is there a structural criterion for the tensor product A ⊗_F B of two F-division algebras A and B to have a zero divisor?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s exact target: it is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Section 9, Problem 9.1 (p. 25). It correctly identifies the ambient tensor product A ⊗_F B, the inputs A and B as F-division algebras, and the precise phenomenon the paper asks about, namely whether the tensor product has a zero divisor.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the term "F-division algebra" should be unpacked using the paper’s background definition: an F-division algebra is a finite-dimensional central simple F-algebra with no nontrivial one-sided ideals (Section 0, Basic definitions, p. 2).
The field F should be stated explicitly as arbitrary; Problem 9.1 does not impose extra hypotheses on characteristic, degree, period, index, or roots of unity (Section 9, Problem 9.1, p. 25).

The variables should be explicitly quantified as two given F-division algebras A and B, so the question reads as a general criterion problem rather than an informal observation about one tensor product (Section 9, Problem 9.1, p. 25).

To stay paper-faithful, the question should not be sharpened into a criterion involving common maximal subfields or common splitting fields; those are treated separately as Problems 9.2 and 9.3, not as equivalent reformulations of Problem 9.1 (Section 9, Problems 9.2-9.3, pp. 25-26).

If context is included, it should be only the paper’s immediate motivation: Section 9 frames Problem 9.1 as part of the decomposability problem for division algebras, after recalling that the interesting cases arise beyond the routine p-primary equal-period/equal-index situation (Section 9 opening paragraph, p. 25).
refined_question: Let F be a field, and let A and B be finite-dimensional central simple F-algebras that are division algebras. Find a structural criterion that characterizes exactly when the tensor product A ⊗_F B contains a nonzero zero divisor.
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 9 rather than the earlier conjectures and theorems: its wording matches Section 9, Problem 9.1 almost exactly (p. 25). The only paper-critical additions needed for a fully stand-alone formulation are the background definition of an F-division algebra from Section 0 (p. 2) and the scope boundary that Problem 9.1 is the broad tensor-product criterion question, while the nearby symbol-algebra/common-maximal-subfield and splitting-field variants are separate Problems 9.2 and 9.3 (pp. 25-26). The surrounding "What is known" discussion also explains why one should not collapse Problem 9.1 into a common-maximal-subfield criterion: that works for quaternions but fails in higher-degree examples (Section 9, "What is known," p. 26).
